questions: If the bottom row is not completely filled, are any blocks removed at that time step, or is the removal step skipped entirely?
When checking “the entire bottom row is filled,” does this refer to all W columns being occupied by at least one block, regardless of multiple blocks stacked in the same column?
During the “order from bottom to top” processing, how is the ordering defined when multiple blocks share the same y‑coordinate but are in different columns?
If a block moves downward into a cell that was just vacated by another block earlier in the same time step, is that allowed, or must the moved block wait until the next time step?

After the removal of the bottom row (if it occurs), does the “order from bottom to top” start with the new bottom row of the remaining blocks, or is the ordering based on the original positions before removal?
Are blocks allowed to occupy the same cell simultaneously at any point, or is such a situation prohibited by the movement rules?

When a query asks whether block A_j exists at time T_j, does “exists” mean the block has not been removed by the bottom‑row deletion rule up to and including time T_j, or does it also require the block to be present after the movement phase of time T_j?
Are the time steps indexed starting from t = 1 after the initial configuration at t = 0, and does the process described (removal then movement) occur exactly once per integer time t up to 10^{100}?

inline_prompts: There is a grid with 10^9 rows and W columns. The cell at the x-th column from the left and the y-th row from the bottom is denoted by (x,y). There are N blocks. Each block is a 1 \times 1 square, and block i-th (1 \leq i \leq N) is located at cell (X_i,Y_i) at time 0. At times t=1,2,\dots,10^{100}, the blocks are moved according to the following rules: - If the entire bottom row is filled with blocks, then all blocks in the bottom row are removed. - For each remaining block, in order from bottom to top, perform the following: - If the block is in the bottom row, or if there is a block in the cell immediately below it, do nothing. - Otherwise, move the block one cell downward. You are given Q queries. For the j-th query (1 \leq j \leq Q), answer whether block A_j exists at time T_j. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N W X_1 Y_1 X_2 Y_2 \vdots X_N Y_N Q T_1 A_1 T_2 A_2 \vdots T_Q A_Q Output Print Q lines. Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq W \leq N - 1 \leq X_i \leq W - 1 \leq Y_i \leq 10^9 - (X_i,Y_i) \neq (X_j,Y_j) if i \neq j. - 1 \leq Q \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq T_j \leq 10^9 - 1 \leq A_j \leq N - All input values are integers.
